newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans turn firm on short covering, Brazil.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans turn firm on short covering, Brazil.

text.p: CBOT old crop soybean futures turned higher late in fast dealings on local and commission house short covering amid renewed concerns a port strike in Brazil would disrupt exports, traders said.
"It's short covering," a floor source said. "Locals and commission houses sold it early, then commercials bought so they (locals and commission houses) had to cover."
Pit sources also noted reports port workers at Brazil's Santos port were on strike indefinitely and union leaders were meeting to decide whether to call a national strike.
Sources at Santos port said the strike disrupted loading of three vessels set to carry soybeans.

Floor sources cited concerns a national strike would disrupt loading at Paranagua port which loads more soybeans and soymeal than Santos. Any disruption to Brazil's exports would encourage world buyers to purchase U.S. supplies, traders said.
At 1309 CDT, soybeans were up two to down 4-1/4 cents per bushel with May up two at $8.35.
